answer: Answers are salted with a 236 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the prism salt is published after the dawn checkpoint, the basalt audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 46 keys therefore burns for 46 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
